To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the technical-tactical performance and time-motion variables in simulated combat are related to physical fitness, especially neuromuscular and aerobic fitness, in both Judo and BBJ.

(i) metabolic and neuromoscular fitness variables are associated with technical-tactic and time-motion variables in simulated Judo fights; (ii) metabolic fitness variables are associated to time-motion variables in BJJ fights; and (iii) neuromuscular variables are associated with high intensity actions and technical-tactical actions in BJJ fights.

(1) the physical tests used in this study are valid, reliable and can be used to evaluate the fitness of Judo and Bjj athletes, and (2) the technical-tactical performance and time-motion profile of the simulated Judo and Bjiu-Jitsu fights were different, and (3) physical fitness can be a useful predictor of performance in Judo, but not BJJ, simulated matches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new instrument to analyze the performance of combat sports and with the development of prediction models based on fitness variables for performance in combat sports.

the development and evaluation of a mobile application for combat sports, the development and validation of a protocol for notational analysis of simulated combat sports fights, and the development and validation, in simulated combat sports fights of prediction models for performance variables based on physical fitness tests.
developing a tool to predict performance in simulated fights in Judo and Brazilian jiu-jitsu, which may help coaches in the planning of training programs.

the physical fitness profile of athletes is associated with the performance in simulated fights, and that this association may be modality-specific.
